messages:
lina.s: Escalating a customer private deployment issue (Acme Prod). They get intermittent 502s from our hosted gateway when routed via their Direct Connect + customer firewall. Customer reports TLS handshake failures in their app logs and DNS NXDOMAIN for internal resolvers. IPsec/VC peer shows tunnel UP. Pls triage.

matthew.c: Ok — can you paste the customer-observed client error and any IKE/ipsec logs you have? Also which subnets/VPCs are impacted?

lina.s: From customer SRE (pasted):
```
2026-03-15T14:12:02Z ERROR api.gateway connect: TLS handshake failed: tls: unexpected SNI \"\" (local: \"acme.prod.example\")
2026-03-15T14:12:02Z WARN resolve: lookup service.internal.acme on 169.254.169.254:53: no such host
```
They say this started after a firewall firmware push. They can still ping the gateway IP over the Direct Connect, but application-level TLS hangs ~500ms then 502. They verified IPsec tunnel shows SA ESTABLISHED on both ends.

raja.k: Two quick checks: 1) Are UDP 4500/500 and ESP (50) allowed through the customer's firewall/NAT for NAT-T? 2) Are we seeing any MTU / DF-bit drops across the DX path?

lina.s: Customer confirmed UDP 500/4500 allowed. They said they blocked ESP during test (to try NAT-T), but current policy allows ESP. MTU suspicion: they bumped MTU on the firewall to 9000 recently.

derek.infra: Large MTU can break TLS over IPsec if PMTUD is blocked. Ask them to try forcing DF=0 or set MTU to 1500 on the firewall for a quick test. Also check if the firewall is rewriting SNI (some proxies can strip SNI) — that would cause tls: unexpected SNI "".

lina.s: Customer ran tcpdump at their edge. Snippet they provided:
```
# sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 54.210.33.12 and port 443
15:10:02.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.52344 > 54.210.33.12.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240
15:10:02.234567 IP 54.210.33.12.443 > 10.0.5.12.52344: Flags [S.], seq 54321, ack 12346
15:10:02.345678 IP 10.0.5.12.52344 > 54.210.33.12.443: Flags [P.], ack 54322, length 0
# then no TLS ClientHello, reset seen later
```
They claim the client never sends the TLS ClientHello byte sequence (or it's being dropped).

raja.k: That lines up with middlebox dropping large fragments or blocking long UDP/ESP flows. Can confirm on our egress logs if we see incomplete TCP connections from their source IPs. Lina, can you share the source IP/CIDR and the exact Direct Connect / VPC route table entries so I can trace?

lina.s: Provided: src CIDR 10.0.5.0/24; our egress IP for that tenant: 54.210.33.12; VPC route table has a route to the VGW pointing to the DX virtual interface.

support-bot: New attachment: acme-prod-vpn-logs.tar.gz (uploaded)

derek.infra: Also check customer OCSP/CRL egress — if OCSP queries go to a blocked resolver, TLS handshakes can stall. Which outbound DNS are they using? If they were using 169.254.169.254 stub resolver (as in logs) that suggests an internal resolver issue.

lina.s: Customer says the firewall now intercepts DNS and forwards to an internal DNS appliance; when we queried that appliance it returned SERVFAIL for our ocsp responder domain. They also saw their firewall rewrite SNI for some hosts during TLS inspection.

raja.k: Action items: 1) Have customer temporarily bypass TLS inspection for our customer gateway IPs (54.210.33.12/28) 2) Force MTU to 1500 on the firewall to see if PMTUD issues resolve 3) Ensure their DNS allows resolution to our OCSP/CRL endpoints and to public root servers.

ops_oncall: I'll add a short-lived exception in our routing/logging to capture full packet traces from our side for the impacted tenant. @derek.infra can you watch for retransmit/dup acks and any TCP MSS clamping?

derek.infra: Yep — watching. Preliminary from our side shows SYN, SYN-ACK, then client pushes an empty TCP packet (no data). Could be middlebox doing inline reassembly or dropping segments over the path.

lina.s: Customer accepted the bypass test; they reported immediate improvement after removing TLS inspection: requests started succeeding and SNI shows correctly. They will schedule a firewall config rollback and plan to add explicit allowlist entries for our OCSP/responder IPs and restore MTU to 1500 while they test.

matthew.c: Good root cause candidate: firewall TLS inspection + MTU change + internal DNS blocking OCSP led to handshake failures and apparent 502s. Next steps for us: document recommended egress allowlist and MTU warning in the Private deployment onboarding KB, and add a monitoring alert for anomalous SNI-empty TLS handshakes.

lina.s: Filed support ticket SR-2026-3145 and updated customer. Marking as resolved pending their firewall patch schedule. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Ticket SR-2026-3145 created and linked to account: acme-prod

ops_oncall: please ping if it recurs after their patch. :thumbsup:
